deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. This page is a working sheet from Gauss's goniometric measurement of the angle between two faces of a crystal. The next page mentions aragonite and calcite (Kalkspath). The method is reflection: a theodolite views, by reflection in the two crystal faces, two distant marks A and A'. The page has three parts.

(I) REPETITION MEASUREMENT.
- Theodolite readings on the marks: A = 355°7'0", A' = 79°33'40". Their difference is 79°33'40" + 360° - 355°7'0" = 84°26'40". This is the angle at the instrument between the two marks.
- Eleven successive circle readings of the repeated reflected angle: 311°35'40", 37°21'15", 123°5'40", 208°51'30", 294°36'5", 20°20'55", 106°5'50", 191°51'15", 277°36'30", 3°21'45", 89°6'10".
- Successive differences (mod 360°) are written in the right column: 85°45'35", 44'25", 45'50", 44'35", 44'50", 44'55", 45'25", 45'15", 45'15", 44'25".
- Mean: (89°6'10" + 3·360° - 311°35'40")/10 = 857°30'30"/10 = 85°45'3".

(II) DISTANCES OF THE MARKS.
- Distance of A: R = cot(2°21'25")/cos(1°29'22") + 0.2724.
  - log cot 2°21'25" = 1.3855282 and log cos 1°29'22" = 9.9998532 - 10, so the quotient is 24.3038.
  - Adding AB = 0.2724 m (given on the previous page) gives R = 24.5762 m, with log R = 1.39051.
- Distance of A': R' = ½ cot(1°34'55").
  - 1°34'55" is half of 152°33'55" - 149°24'5" = 3°9'50", the angle subtended by a 1 m rod ("Meter bei A'" on the previous page).
  - log cot = 1.5588210, so log R' = 1.2577910 and R' = 18.105 m.

(III) ECCENTRICITY / PARALLAX CORRECTION.
The reflecting point of the crystal lies a small distance e from the instrument axis.
- log e = 8.50447 - 9.99985 = 8.50462 - 10, so e ≈ 0.03196 m (the division by a cosine is a slope reduction).
- Each mark then suffers an angular shift of order ρ e/r, with ρ = 206264.8" and log ρ = 5.31443.
- The amplitudes are:
  - a = ρ/R: log 5.31443 - 1.39051 = 3.92392, a = 8393".
  - b = ρ/R': log 5.31443 - 1.25779 = 4.05664, b = 11393".
- The marks lie at directions ∓A from their bisector, with 2A ≈ 84°26'28" (the A-A' angle), so A = 42°13'14".
- The two sinusoidal shifts are combined into one sinusoid using the formula at the bottom of the page.
  - Phase: tan T = ((b-a)/(b+a)) tan A, giving T = 7°50'2". My check gives 7°49'58".
  - Amplitude: log[(a+b) cos A/(2 cos T)] = 3.86896. My check gives 3.86893.
  - Times e: log C = 3.86896 + 8.50462 - 10 = 2.37358, so C = 236.4".
- Orientation: α = 45°10'22" plus Const = 107°16'28" gives 152°26'50". This is the 'k = 152°26'50"' of the previous page. Dependence on the end readings λ (311°35'40" and 37°21'15") comes in through this orientation.
- C is multiplied by two trigonometric factors (log 9.93247 and log 9.76258), giving 202.32" and 136.82". Their difference is 65.50".
- Hence the correction is ∓65.5":
  - 85°45'3" - 65.5" = 85°43'57" 'nach dem Protocoll' (k as recorded);
  - 85°45'3" + 65.5" = 85°46'9" 'nach dem Augenmaß' (k + 180°, as the previous page notes).
  The exact arguments of the two trig factors are not decodable with certainty from the page.

(IV) AUXILIARY LEMMA (the method used in III).
It is to be read as: a(cos A - i sin A) + b(cos A + i sin A) = t(cos T + i sin T), i.e. a e^{-iA} + b e^{iA} = t e^{iT}. Then:
1) tan T = tan A / ((b+a)/(b-a)). This is the real/imaginary parts (a+b)cos A and (b-a)sin A.
2) t = a sin 2A / sin(A-T) = b sin 2A / sin(A+T). Proof (my filling): multiply by e^{-iA} and take imaginary parts, t sin(T-A) = -a sin 2A. Multiply by e^{iA}, t sin(T+A) = b sin 2A.
Equivalently, a sin(x-A) + b sin(x+A) = t sin(x+T): two sinusoids of the same period combine into one, here applied to the two parallactic terms.
errors: No arithmetic error found in the repetition differences or the mean 85°45'3".
T: recomputation gives 7°49'58" against Gauss's 7°50'2", a difference of a few seconds within log-table precision. The amplitude log checks to about 3e-5.

Previous-page discrepancy: the rod readings 'bei A' are transcribed as 66°2'20" and 67°23'45" (difference 1°21'25"), whereas this page uses 2°21'25". This is likely a misreading there (68°23'45"?) or a different reduction. Unsure.
The first line of the complex formula as written ('b+ a cos A ...') contains a stray or struck 'b+'. Only a e^{-iA} + b e^{iA} is consistent with formulas 1) and 2), which are correct.

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine observational reduction: a repetition mean, subtense distances, and an eccentricity correction via phasor addition. Gauss's crystallographic interests (cf. his 1831 Seeber review) and his habitual use of complex numbers are known. The only mild interest is seeing him use a complex-number lemma inside a practical crystal-goniometry reduction.

Formula 2) as transcribed (t = a sin 2A/sin(A-T) = b sin 2A/sin(A+T)) matches the image and is correct.
